query: in the side-by-side spec view, how does the app decide which handset is the better one for a given row?
why: Only file implementing winner selection: higher/lower-is-better keyword lists, resolutions compared by total pixels, delta badge with units.

query: will the site keep serving pages if the cache server is unreachable?
why: Sole place documenting that Keyv is built with throwOnConnectError/throwOnErrors disabled so a dead Redis degrades to cache misses instead of 500s.

query: raw model strings arrive full of region tags, network bands and storage sizes — where do they get cleaned into proper product names?
why: cleanName() is the only logic stripping network tokens, country codes, capacity suffixes and alias fragments from model strings.

query: how is the little up/down arrow next to a device's price worked out?
why: getPriceTrend compares the two most recent entries and returns trend plus percentage; nothing else computes a direction indicator.

query: before we ship, what known defects and security holes have already been catalogued, and in what order should they be tackled?
why: Only document enumerating confirmed bugs (search 500, broken images, dead price filters, exposed JWT) plus a numbered suggested fix order.

query: does the system pull fresh device data on a schedule without anyone clicking anything?
why: Contains the Sunday 03:00 weekly cron with gap-fill semantics and the 200-device deep-sync batch cap; no other code schedules work.

query: if an admin edits something, could their password end up recorded in the change history?
why: Only file capturing write operations into audit logs, with sanitizeBody masking password/token/secret fields.

query: what URL should a load balancer ping to confirm the app can actually reach its database?
why: Defines /health/live versus /health/ready, where ready checks the Mongo connection state and returns 503 when the DB is down.

query: device pictures from a new image CDN render broken — where do I need to allow that host?
why: Sole location of the next/image remotePatterns allowlist gating which external image hosts may render.

query: when a visitor loses internet, can they still look at specs they already viewed?
why: Service worker implements network-first-then-cache plus old-cache cleanup on activate; the only source of offline browsing behavior.

query: how do we stop a user-typed query containing dots or brackets from breaking pattern matching on the server?
why: Definition site of escapeRegExp, the helper every backend and frontend regex search calls to prevent pattern injection.

query: do accented characters in device names survive when turned into URL identifiers?
why: Only slug helper that NFD-normalizes and strips diacritics before lowercasing; the backend util merely re-exports it.

query: why is the cheapest-offer badge never awarded across two different currencies?
why: buildCurrencyGroups groups offers per currency and picks Best Deal only within a group, explicitly refusing cross-currency conversion.

query: how can shoppers narrow the listing by what a phone costs when the price is not stored on the phone record itself?
why: latestPriceStages shows the Device doc never holds a price, so filtering/sorting requires a $lookup into the price history collection.

query: if a shopper types a long phrase and nothing matches, does search try anything else?
why: Unique fallback that splits a multi-word query into individual words and retries with per-word regexes when the first pass is empty.

query: which screen visualises ad income versus affiliate income over time?
why: Only file using recharts (AreaChart/PieChart) to draw revenue trends and vendor click share on the admin home.

query: is there an automated browser check that a regular visitor can search and land on a device page?
why: The public-journey Playwright spec (search then open a device detail); the only other e2e spec covers admin login instead.

query: what do I need to sign up for, and get approved for, before the site can start earning money?
why: Only guide covering AdSense site approval, ads.txt, Amazon Associates 180-day rule and Jumia/Kolibri signup steps.

query: which phases of the build are still unfinished?
why: Canonical phase checklist showing testing, deployment and growth phases unchecked while earlier phases are done.

query: why can't I just run the API on the same port the frontend dev server uses?
why: Explains the backend deliberately runs on 3001 to avoid colliding with Next.js on 3000, plus workspace/env setup for a new developer.
